page: The Microsoft Azure E64ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv6 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The system provides 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, backed by a 260 MB L3 cache. It features 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, and includes 3780 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong memory read bandwidth, reaching 4509.39 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 246.15 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Multi-core performance is robust, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 72,789.57 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 338.7 GB/sec. Database and caching operations are highly efficient, with the system achieving 84.54 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 28,978.89 in PassMark database tests. Single-core performance and large-block memory write speeds remain in the average tier.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the E64ds_v6 is driven by its high resource density, bundling substantial memory capacity and fast local NVMe storage within a single instance. This configuration reduces the need for external storage attachments for data-heavy operations. The server is well-suited for memory-intensive enterprise applications, relational databases, high-throughput caching layers, and CPU-based large language model inference.
